# Field precision — the mainnet ratchet, labelled

<!-- GENERATED by `python -m tests.mainnet_triage --write-doc`; do not edit by hand. -->

`docs/PRECISION.md` scores each detector on a curated corpus we wrote; it is a
specification, not a field rate. This page is the field number: every finding
cell of the mainnet findings ratchet (211 of the 231 distinct
real mainnet programs in `tests/mainnet-random-probes/` have findings) carries a
truth label in `tests/mainnet_triage.json` — `TP` (real weakness), `FP` (claim
false or provably neutralised), `INTENDED` (true, but the author's evident
design, e.g. creator-gated update or close-out to the creator), `UNKNOWN`
(not decidable from the program text, or not read).

**Coverage:** 1519/1951 cells decided (78%); critical/high cells 817/898 (91%). Overall labelled precision TP/(TP+FP) = 387/739 = 0.52.

> **Caveats.** Precision is over DECIDED cells only — UNKNOWN cells are
> excluded, so a detector with many UNKNOWNs has a wide error bar. `INTENDED`
> counts neither for nor against precision: it is the share of findings a
> reviewer will dismiss as by-design. Labels marked `rule:<class>` were
> extended from a manually-read representative of the same code shape; the
> rest were read individually. The ratchet's 231 programs are a random
> mainnet sample, deduplicated by content hash, not a holdout set.

Sampled rather than fully triaged (cells left unlabelled): `tainted-fund-flow` (32 unlabelled), `tainted-log` (128 unlabelled), `unsafe-division-order` (86 unlabelled), `tainted-state-write` (6 unlabelled), `arbitrary-inner-asset` (3 unlabelled), `arbitrary-inner-appcall` (7 unlabelled).

## False-positive classes

Each FP class with its count and one example (`probe:line`). Classes
marked *fixable* are shapes a detector could recognise from the program
text alone.

### `tainted-fund-flow`

- **pin-to-creator-written-local-state** ×20 — e.g. `app_1050030771.teal:1565`: receiver Accounts[j] asserted == local(Accounts[i]).beneficiary_address; that key is written only in the open handler, which asserts txn Sender == CreatorAddress - the account index is attacker-picked but every candidate value is creator-written *Fixable: receiver pinned to local state whose only writer is creator-gated; the F3 input-vs-input rule fires only because the account index is caller-picked.*
- **payout-backed-by-caller-payment** ×15 — e.g. `app_1300367999.teal:1507`: buy handler asserts the offered btoi(arg1) == the caller's own sibling payment to the app; seller price, commissions and the overpayment refund (to the payer) are all carved out of that payment *Fixable: amount asserted equal to the caller's own payment to the app.*
- **select-between-trusted-arms** ×8 — e.g. `app_1050027991.teal:194`: every callsub of the transfer helper passes close-to = ZeroAddress, load 0 (txn Sender at creation / global 'SL' written only at creation) or select(ZeroAddress, load 0, cond); the attacker only steers the select CONDITION *Fixable: taint from select's CONDITION must not taint the value when both data arms are trusted.*
- **receiver-from-verified-child-app-state** ×8 — e.g. `app_3600022590.teal:357`: transfer helper's call sites pass receivers = app address, global fee_address / market_friend_addr, txn Sender (amount = its own asserted sibling deposit), or the 'owner' of an order app verified as created by this app (AppCreator == app address); the arg only selects WHICH order app
- **sender-pinned-to-trusted-app-address** ×8 — e.g. `app_2200406603.teal:141`: 'transfer' handler asserts txn Sender == app_params_get AppAddress(global 'bid'), the bridge app; 'bid' is set at creation and rotated only by that same app *Fixable via authority layer: app_params_get AppAddress of a preserved app id.*
- **arg-indexed-trusted-state-receiver** ×6 — e.g. `app_1850333786.teal:181`: receivers at every helper call site are the seller/creator (load 0), the asserted winning bidder, txn Sender, or global 'GRA'+itob(arg1) - a royalty address written by LOAD_ROYALTIES from the asset creator's royalty app; the arg only picks WHICH stored entry
- **fee-to-fixed-recipient** ×4 — e.g. `app_1050030771.teal:1957`: fee share paid to app_params_get AppAddress of Applications[122], asserted == constant app 949203488
- **sender-pinned-to-whitelisted-state** ×4 — e.g. `app_2200406603.teal:223`: 'withdraw' requires the preceding txn to be the caller's own call to the bridge app with sender == global w1 or w2 (whitelist written only by the bridge app); payout goes to txn Sender
- **refund-of-freed-box-mbr** ×3 — e.g. `app_2645463331.teal:551`: Amount = sum of 2500+400*(keylen+boxlen) over boxes just box_del'd, paid to txn Sender: exactly the MBR released, the app's spendable balance cannot drop
- **receiver-pinned-to-owner-state** ×3 — e.g. `app_2645463331.teal:3522`: the NFD asa is clawed to frame -2, which the caller (vault_send) asserted == state "i.owner.a" before callsub label119 — the NFD goes to its owner (same code as app_2300200702.teal:3480). Moved from partial-tainted-fund-flow on 2026-10-14 when the owner read became account-typed: the a07 address-pin rule now judges the owner slot, whose writers include `gtxns Sender` of a purchase payment (anyone who buys becomes owner) — authority not preserved, yet the NFD still goes to its rightful owner
- **sender-pinned-to-registry-admin** ×2 — e.g. `app_2450526014.teal:351`: the arg-amount withdraw site asserts txn Sender == the 'MNA' address read from the UL_SUPERADMIN_APP registry app (app_global_get_ex of a foreign admin app) and pays txn Sender
- **signature-verified-payload** ×2 — e.g. `app_2450526014.teal:353`: receiver is field 72..104 of a base64 order payload whose signature is checked by label65 (ed25519verify_bare / ecdsa_verify against the payload's signer) before label90 pays out
- **sender-pinned-to-admin-state** ×2 — e.g. `app_900170865.teal:92`: withdraw asserts (callsub label14) txn Sender == CreatorAddress || == global admin (admin rotated only under the same gate) and pays txn Sender
- **pin-to-verified-child-owner** ×1 — e.g. `app_3600022590.teal:370`: cancel handler asserts the receiver arg == 'owner' of an order app created by this app before the fixed MBR refund; the other caller pays a fixed 10000 uALGO tip to txn Sender

### `is-deletable`

- **oc-test-combined-in-callee** ×4 — e.g. `app_2200207295.teal:143`: this exit is in the OC==0 method arm (bnz label4 after `txn OnCompletion; int 0; ==; callsub label2; callsub label3`); Delete goes only to label8 *Fixable: the OC comparison flows through a callee that returns arg && x; carry the predicate through the callee return value tree.*
- **exit-value-zero-on-path** ×2 — e.g. `app_900033624.teal:2336`: DeleteApplication jumps straight to label2, which pushes 0 and branches to the shared `return` at label10: the Delete path always rejects; the shared exit only approves for other arms. (same shape as app_900032639.teal) *Fixable: judge the verdict operand per incoming edge (Delete jumps to int 0; b shared-return).*
- **assert-false-in-handler** ×1 — e.g. `app_1300010796.teal:94`: the Delete handler (callsub label13) asserts the creator and then executes `pushint 0; assert`, so Delete always fails *Fixable: handler ends in int 0; assert.*

### `inner-txn-close-rekey`

- **close-to-self** ×2 — e.g. `app_3500277892.teal:166`: AssetCloseTo = global CurrentApplicationAddress (receiver also self, amount 0): the asset never leaves the app *Fixable: suppress AssetCloseTo == CurrentApplicationAddress like ZeroAddress.*

### `is-updatable`

- **oc-test-combined-in-callee** ×6 — e.g. `app_2200207295.teal:143`: OC tests are `txn OnCompletion; int K; ==` then `callsub label2; callsub label3` which only && extra txn-field checks; OC==4 goes to label7 `int 0; return`, so Update never approves *Fixable: the OC comparison flows through a callee that returns arg && x; carry the predicate through the callee return value tree.*
- **oc-excluded-on-all-paths** ×2 — e.g. `app_2900566908.teal:9`: every method arm asserts OnCompletion==NoOp except the delete arm (OC==5), and the bare path returns 0 for any OC!=0; Update can never approve *Fixable: same root as retsub-context-merge / router run inside a proto sub.*
- **oc-assert-inside-router-sub** ×1 — e.g. `app_2800792564.teal:9`: Puya router runs as subroutine label3: every method arm asserts OC==0 (`txn OnCompletion; !; assert`) except label18 (OC==5), and the bare route returns 0 — UpdateApplication can never approve at the top-level return *Fixable: OC asserts inside the router subroutine are not seen from the exit after callsub.*
- **assert-false-in-handler** ×1 — e.g. `app_1300010796.teal:102`: the Update handler (callsub label14) asserts the creator and then executes `pushint 0; assert`, so Update always fails *Fixable: handler ends in int 0; assert.*

### `unsafe-division-order`

- **fixed-point-scaled-division** ×4 — e.g. `app_3550277940.teal:1694`: `x*(2^64-1)/y` is a fixed-point ratio later multiplied and rescaled; truncation is 2^-64 relative *Fixable: x*2^64/y before a multiply is fixed-point scaling.*
- **exact-division-by-construction** ×4 — e.g. `app_1050135395.teal:327`: `L*(L+1)/2` is a triangular number, always exact; the /2 truncates nothing before *92
- **result-discarded** ×3 — e.g. `app_1850333786.teal:725`: the `a/b*c` product is immediately `pop`ped; it feeds no value *Fixable: the product is popped.*
- **exact-division-checked** ×2 — e.g. `app_2800637334.teal:151`: `qty = Amount/price` then `Amount == qty*price` is asserted: the multiply IS the exactness check *Fixable: q = a/b followed by assert a == q*b is an exactness check.*

### `delete-funds-check`

- **oc-test-combined-in-callee** ×4 — e.g. `app_2200207295.teal:143`: this exit is in the OC==0 method arm (bnz label4 after `txn OnCompletion; int 0; ==; callsub label2; callsub label3`); Delete goes only to label8 *Fixable: the OC comparison flows through a callee that returns arg && x; carry the predicate through the callee return value tree.*
- **delete-drains-first** ×2 — e.g. `app_1050027991.teal:929`: the delete path calls label43, which closes the app ALGO remainder (CloseRemainderTo) to the seller before approving *Fixable: accept a CloseRemainderTo/AssetCloseTo inner txn dominating the delete exit as balance handling.*
- **exit-value-zero-on-path** ×2 — e.g. `app_900033624.teal:2336`: DeleteApplication jumps straight to label2, which pushes 0 and branches to the shared `return` at label10: the Delete path always rejects; the shared exit only approves for other arms. (same shape as app_900032639.teal) *Fixable: judge the verdict operand per incoming edge (Delete jumps to int 0; b shared-return).*
- **delete-checks-balance** ×1 — e.g. `app_750699088.teal:99`: This Delete exit is reached only when the app balance is <= 1000 microAlgo (otherwise it closes out to the creator): a balance check the detector does not recognise. *Fixable: a balance <= K bound before deleting (close-out otherwise) is balance handling; the detector accepts only a direct balance-vs-min_balance comparison (its README still describes an opcode-presence proxy).*
- **assert-false-in-handler** ×1 — e.g. `app_1300010796.teal:94`: the Delete handler (callsub label13) asserts the creator and then executes `pushint 0; assert`, so Delete always fails *Fixable: handler ends in int 0; assert.*
- **balance-check-via-acct-params** ×1 — e.g. `app_2800567692.teal:9`: label33 asserts AcctBalance - AcctMinBalance == 0 via acct_params_get before deleting; the detector only recognises the balance/min_balance opcodes *Fixable: accept acct_params_get AcctBalance/AcctMinBalance as the balance pair.*

### `timelock-upgrade`

- **oc-test-combined-in-callee** ×5 — e.g. `app_2200207295.teal:143`: OC tests are `txn OnCompletion; int K; ==` then `callsub label2; callsub label3` which only && extra txn-field checks; OC==4 goes to label7 `int 0; return`, so Update never approves *Fixable: the OC comparison flows through a callee that returns arg && x; carry the predicate through the callee return value tree.*
- **timelock-present** ×2 — e.g. `app_900033624.teal:2336`: Update requires "cut" != 0 and cut <= LatestTimestamp, and "scu" only sets cut >= LatestTimestamp + "cud" (delay read from the governance app): a real timelock the detector misses. (same shape as app_900032639.teal)
- **assert-false-in-handler** ×1 — e.g. `app_1300010796.teal:102`: the Update handler (callsub label14) asserts the creator and then executes `pushint 0; assert`, so Update always fails *Fixable: handler ends in int 0; assert.*

### `unprotected-deletable`

- **creator-or-foreign-admin-gate-missed** ×3 — e.g. `app_3400287920.teal:60`: delete method asserts OC==5; its helper asserts txn Sender == CreatorAddress || the market app's "escrow_cancel_address" *Fixable via authority layer (foreign-app admin).*
- **exit-value-zero-on-path** ×2 — e.g. `app_900033624.teal:2336`: DeleteApplication jumps straight to label2, which pushes 0 and branches to the shared `return` at label10: the Delete path always rejects; the shared exit only approves for other arms. (same shape as app_900032639.teal) *Fixable: judge the verdict operand per incoming edge (Delete jumps to int 0; b shared-return).*
- **foreign-app-admin-gate-missed** ×2 — e.g. `app_2450526014.teal:612`: Delete asserts Sender == app_global_get_ex(UL_SUPERADMIN_APP, "MNA"), a real admin gate held in a creation-set governance app; the detector only credits creator/own-state pins. *Fixable via authority layer: admin read from an app id written only at creation/under creator pin.*
- **foreign-registry-role-gate** ×1 — e.g. `app_3450330087.teal:1678`: Delete requires Sender == "xgov_daemon" read via app_global_get_ex from the registry app (label50/label22) — an authority check through foreign state the creator-only rule cannot see
- **creator-gate-inside-nested-sub** ×1 — e.g. `app_2800792564.teal:9`: Delete arm label18 (inside router sub label3) calls label33 which asserts Sender == CreatorAddress before anything else; the gate sits two calls deep
- **oc-test-combined-in-callee** ×1 — e.g. `app_2200207295.teal:211`: this exit is in the OC==0 method arm (bnz label4 after `txn OnCompletion; int 0; ==; callsub label2; callsub label3`); Delete goes only to label8 *Fixable: the OC comparison flows through a callee that returns arg && x; carry the predicate through the callee return value tree.*
- **fixed-address-signed-sibling-gate** ×1 — e.g. `app_203455577.teal:70`: Delete requires gtxn 2 Sender == one of three hardcoded addresses (assert at 33) — an authority check the creator-only rule does not recognise
- **admin-key-gate-missed** ×1 — e.g. `app_3550180073.teal:138`: Update/Delete call label21 which asserts Sender == global "g"; "g" is written only at creation and by a method that first runs the same assert, so the admin is preserved.
- **creator-gated-delete-missed** ×1 — e.g. `app_2800567692.teal:9`: the only Delete arm (label7, OC==5) calls label33, which asserts txn Sender == global CreatorAddress
- **reach-participant-gate** ×1 — e.g. `app_1050058216.teal:3059`: Reach delete path (label13, phase load 1 == 2) asserts Sender is one of the two participant addresses held in global state (load 255 / load 251, or load 251 alone on label89), then asserts OC==5 and closes assets and ALGO to the creator — not deletable by anyone
- **owner-multisig-gate-missed** ×1 — e.g. `app_900123673.teal:1283`: Delete calls label18 (rejects unless txn Sender equals one of the stored "owner_N" addresses) and asserts the recorded approvals >= global "thres"

### `unprotected-updatable`

- **foreign-app-admin-gate-missed** ×5 — e.g. `app_3400287920.teal:48`: update method asserts OC==4; its helper asserts txn Sender == the parent market app's global "market_friend_addr" (market_app_id = CallerApplicationID at creation) *Fixable via authority layer: admin read from an app id written only at creation/under creator pin.*
- **oc-excluded-on-all-paths** ×2 — e.g. `app_2900566908.teal:9`: every method arm asserts OnCompletion==NoOp except the delete arm (OC==5), and the bare path returns 0 for any OC!=0; Update can never approve *Fixable: same root as retsub-context-merge / router run inside a proto sub.*
- **oc-assert-inside-router-sub** ×1 — e.g. `app_2800792564.teal:9`: Puya router runs as subroutine label3: every method arm asserts OC==0 (`txn OnCompletion; !; assert`) except label18 (OC==5), and the bare route returns 0 — UpdateApplication can never approve at the top-level return *Fixable: OC asserts inside the router subroutine are not seen from the exit after callsub.*
- **admin-role-local-state-gate-missed** ×1 — e.g. `app_177244932.teal:107`: Update approves only if the sender's local "roles" has bit 8 (contract admin); the creator gets roles=15 at creation and grantRoles itself requires bit 8
- **oc-test-combined-in-callee** ×1 — e.g. `app_2200207295.teal:211`: OC tests are `txn OnCompletion; int K; ==` then `callsub label2; callsub label3` which only && extra txn-field checks; OC==4 goes to label7 `int 0; return`, so Update never approves *Fixable: the OC comparison flows through a callee that returns arg && x; carry the predicate through the callee return value tree.*
- **admin-key-gate-missed** ×1 — e.g. `app_3550180073.teal:138`: Update/Delete call label21 which asserts Sender == global "g"; "g" is written only at creation and by a method that first runs the same assert, so the admin is preserved.

### `inner-txn-fee`

- **inner-sender-is-caller** ×2 — e.g. `app_1850858495.teal:235`: the inner axfer sets itxn_field Sender = txn Sender (a rekeyed caller account), so the 1000 fee is paid by the caller, not by the application account *Fixable: itxn Sender = txn Sender (rekeyed caller) means the caller pays the fee.*
- **dead-fee-branch** ×1 — e.g. `app_3350348253.teal:207`: MinTxnFee is written only on the switch arm for fee-source 1, but every one of the 12 callers of this op-up helper passes intc_0 (0), selecting the Fee 0 arm *Fixable: constant call arguments select a different switch arm.*

### `group-size-check`

- **gtxn-reads-under-groupsize-branch** ×9 — e.g. `app_250268159.teal:426`: every absolute gtxn read on paths to this exit sits under a global GroupSize==k branch, so the group is pinned wherever a sibling is read *Fixable with per-path gating (exit-path-reads-no-absolute-gtxn).*
- **shared-exit-gtxn-paths-bounded** ×8 — e.g. `app_1100070621.teal:568`: shared exit: every handler that reads gtxn 0/4 asserts GroupSize (==2||==3, ==3, ==5) before reaching it; only gtxn-free handlers (create/opt-in/admin) reach it unbounded *Fixable with per-path gating (exit-path-reads-no-absolute-gtxn).*
- **side-effect-free-method** ×4 — e.g. `app_1300665167.teal:184`: read-only validation method: asserts sibling shapes and logs, no state write or inner txn, so padding or sibling reuse gains nothing
- **groupsize-bounded-on-path** ×4 — e.g. `app_900123673.teal:835`: the method asserts GroupSize (==2/==3/==4) right after common helper calls and before every gtxn read and the exit; walk escapes via the shared helpers *Fixable: the backward walk leaves a shared helper through a different call site; needs a return stack (same as UGS _gate_free_exit_through).*
- **groupsize-branch-guard-missed** ×3 — e.g. `app_151644583.teal:125`: exit is reachable only through bnz on a GroupSize==2 && ... conjunction; the group is pinned *Fixable: root cause not isolated; bnz on GroupSize==K in subroutine-free v2 code.*
- **sibling-read-is-signer-authority** ×2 — e.g. `app_203455577.teal:70`: GroupIndex == 0 is asserted and the only absolute sibling read is gtxn 2 Sender pinned to one of three fixed co-signer addresses (GroupSize >= 3): padding cannot change what was checked
- **sibling-reuse-harmless** ×2 — e.g. `app_3500277892.teal:1374`: OptIn handler only requires gtxn 1 to be an opt_in_offer NoOp call; the effect is the caller opting itself in, idempotent and harmless under padding
- **exit-path-reads-no-absolute-gtxn** ×2 — e.g. `app_900123673.teal:696`: no absolute gtxn/gtxna/gtxnas read on any entry-to-exit path (callees included, call/return matched); padding cannot change what this path checked *Fixable: gate per exit on an absolute gtxn read lying on the entry->exit path, not on the program containing one.*

### `unvalidated-group-sibling`

- **sibling-is-outflow-from-escrow** ×19 — e.g. `app_600334957.teal:278`: gtxn 2 is the escrow refunding the previous "Highest bidder" (Sender == Escrow, Receiver == Highest bidder, Amount == Highest bid) *Fixable: skip a pair whose Sender is pinned to the app / a stored escrow — it is an outflow, not a credit.*
- **receiver-pinned-to-managed-app-address** ×8 — e.g. `app_1300665167.teal:1613`: receivers pinned to addresses derived from "lp_interface_app_id"/"admin_app_id" (set only on the creation call to apps whose AppCreator is the sender) or their state *Fixable via authority layer: creation-only writers preserve authority.*
- **zero-amount-sibling-not-credit** ×6 — e.g. `app_1050043795.teal:84`: gtxn 1 is an opt-in: Sender == AssetReceiver and AssetAmount == 0 asserted — nothing is credited *Fixable: AssetAmount == 0 / Sender == Receiver siblings credit nothing.*
- **receiver-pinned-to-stored-escrow** ×4 — e.g. `app_282499111.teal:189`: bid path checks gtxn 1 Receiver == state "Escrow" (label35) before crediting; Escrow is a logicsig written by a one-shot create
- **receiver-pin-in-returned-boolean** ×4 — e.g. `app_2200117730.teal:801`: same helper as app_1050027265:785: AssetReceiver == CurrentApplicationAddress in the same && chain as the amount read *Fixable: the pin is in the same && chain as the read, returned through retsub.*
- **receiver-pinned-to-party** ×2 — e.g. `app_3350348253.teal:4244`: loan disbursement: the lender pays the borrower directly; the receiver is asserted == state "addrb" (a P2P transfer, not a credit to the app)
- **escrow-setup-funding** ×2 — e.g. `app_151644583.teal:102`: creator-only setup (gtxn 0 Sender == "Creator") funding the escrow named in ApplicationArgs 0, then stored as "AssetEscrow"; not a credit

### `tainted-state-write`

- **member-gated-key** ×8 — e.g. `app_900123673.teal:690`: multisig-style app: label18 rejects (return 0) any Sender not in "owner_N"; keys are proposal names chosen by owners and must already hold a 120-byte proposal record
- **constant-prefix-key-namespace** ×6 — e.g. `app_1850333786.teal:966`: key = "GRA"||arg1: the constant 3-byte prefix confines the write to the per-item royalty cache, refreshed from the asset creator's own local state — no admin/owner key ("ST","SL","FA",...) shares the prefix (same code as app_1050051479.teal:963)
- **scratch-store-from-other-path** ×6 — e.g. `app_1850333786.teal:1161`: key = "GRP"||itob(i) with i a loop index from state "NOA" on a path asserting NumAppArgs == 0 and Sender == "SL"; the ApplicationArgs source is a store to slot 13 on a different method path (same code as app_1050051479.teal:1158) *Fixable: the reaching store of the scratch slot is a constant on this path.*
- **key-from-constant-table** ×3 — e.g. `app_3550180073.teal:419`: key = "t"||substring3("01234p", i, i+1)||suffix: substring3 panics outside the 6-char constant, so the key set is fixed (t0_ra..tp_lp)
- **bounded-key-component** ×2 — e.g. `app_2200606875.teal:1993`: ve-lock slope-change bucket "sc"||itob(t): every caller passes an unlock time asserted to be a multiple of 604800 and within [now+4w, now+~4y] (label22 / label24) or read back from the user's validated lock box
- **sender-pinned-to-foreign-admin-app** ×2 — e.g. `app_2450560800.teal:887`: label74 asserts Sender == "MNA" of the superadmin app (label30) before the TokenManager box write
- **key-validated-against-trusted-app** ×1 — e.g. `app_3550011936.teal:482`: decrement of listing counter "as"||itob(asset): both callers first assert the listing app was created by this app (AppCreator == CurrentApplicationAddress) and its "asset" global == the asset
- **admin-gated-namespaced-key** ×1 — e.g. `app_177244932.teal:198`: setTransferRule: requires the caller's local "roles" bit 2 (granted by admins) and the key is "rule"||itob(from)||itob(to) — a constant-prefixed rule table

### `arbitrary-inner-asset`

- **foreign-array-pinned-to-state** ×8 — e.g. `app_3100284609.teal:1118`: every caller asserts the (g)txn Assets/Accounts/Applications entries == own state ("A","B","LP","POOL_ADDR",...) on the same transaction before calling the transfer helper; amounts are the caller's own deposits
- **asset-goes-to-creator** ×5 — e.g. `app_1100218544.teal:1846`: amount 0 with AssetCloseTo = global CreatorAddress and receiver = the app: the holding can only go to the creator
- **asset-optin-zero-amount-self** ×4 — e.g. `app_2450526014.teal:349`: flagged flow (label210) is an admin-gated (Sender == "BKA") opt-in: amount 0 to CurrentApplicationAddress *Fixable: XferAsset of 0 to the app's own address with no close is an opt-in, not an outflow.*
- **zero-amount-transfer** ×2 — e.g. `app_1850858495.teal:228`: AssetAmount is never set (defaults to 0) and there is no AssetCloseTo: the transfer moves nothing
- **asset-id-from-own-state** ×2 — e.g. `app_3200474904.teal:1339`: load 251 on this path is extract_uint64 of the app's own global state blob (0x00||0x01||0x02) at 314
- **asset-checked-or-to-creator** ×2 — e.g. `app_1700323838.teal:231`: claim path asserts txna Assets 0 == state "plaus_asa_id" before label18 (533-538); activate path is creator-gated and sends to "plaus_creator_address"
- **sender-pinned-to-admin-state** ×1 — e.g. `app_2001600350.teal:128`: label23 asserts txn Sender == state "manager" (set to CreatorAddress at creation) before label18

### `abi-method-selector`

- **reach-btoi-dispatch** ×9 — e.g. `app_1900092936.teal:1171`: Reach router: btoi(arg0) dispatched by a `<` binary-search tree ending in `==; assert`, so unknown selectors abort; the detector does not see pins through btoi/range compares *Fixable: credit a btoi(arg0) dispatch tree ending in ==; assert as a selector pin.*
- **selector-pin-in-conjunction** ×4 — e.g. `app_1300367999.teal:344`: every NoOp route is `arg0 == "name" && NumAppArgs == k; bnz` ending in err; the pin sits inside && so the per-edge selector check never sees it *Fixable: decompose && chains when looking for the selector pin.*
- **selector-pin-in-disjunction** ×4 — e.g. `app_900033624.teal:2336`: string router `arg0 == "sfe" || arg0 == "sef"; bnz` feeds the shared exit; every other string branch errs on no match *Fixable: an || of selector pins is a pin on every arm.*
- **selector-checked-in-callee** ×3 — e.g. `app_2645463331.teal:3897`: ARC4 `match` falls through to `callsub` a legacy string router that compares arg0 to "gas"/"update_field"/... and ends in err; the selector check lives in the callee *Fixable: callee err/return-0 fallthrough rejects unmatched selectors.*
- **router-verdict-via-retsub** ×3 — e.g. `app_2800792564.teal:9`: PuyaPy approval_program sub: unmatched selector after `match` returns `intc_0; retsub` (0) and the program exit `return`s that verdict *Fixable: judge the exit by verdict_operand; a const-0 phi arm is not approving.*
- **lifecycle-oc-path** ×2 — e.g. `app_2200207295.teal:324`: exit is in the creator-gated DeleteApplication handler (label8); the OC==5 test is ANDed with RekeyTo/CloseTo checks inside callsubs so the OC predicate is invisible *Fixable: close the per-edge walk also on edges that exclude NoOp (predicates_exclude_action(conds, 0)) and on the creation path.*
- **btoi-selector-compare** ×1 — e.g. `app_3100297243.teal:148`: exit reached only by OptIn/CloseOut/Update or by handlers routed on `btoi(arg0) == K` (unknown selectors go to label4/label8); the pin goes through btoi *Fixable: same root as reach-btoi-dispatch.*

### `partial-tainted-fund-flow`

- **receiver-from-keyed-record** ×8 — e.g. `app_3550011936.teal:387`: receiver = the depositor address stored in box "as"||asset (written from txn Sender at 305-312); the caller only picks which listing to settle
- **value-from-app-written-record** ×4 — e.g. `app_1050030771.teal:1569`: refund of the order account's own recorded "amount_in"/"asset_in_id" (app-written local state), after creator or expiry, to the recorded "beneficiary_address" (asserted 1537-1544)
- **receiver-pinned-to-constant-app** ×4 — e.g. `app_1050030771.teal:1959`: receiver load 140 = AppAddress of Applications[i], asserted == constant app 949203488 at 1894-1898
- **same-slot-reread-not-credited** ×3 — e.g. `app_1850552146.teal:381`: AssetReceiver = txnas Accounts[frame -3], and the same Accounts[frame -3] is asserted == global CreatorAddress at 351-355; the re-read through a fresh txnas is not credited *Fixable: a fresh txnas of the same (param) slot should share the check.*
- **receiver-is-own-child-app** ×2 — e.g. `app_3550011936.teal:603`: receiver = AppAddress of the listing app, asserted to be created by this app (AppCreator == CurrentApplicationAddress at 564-569)

### `arbitrary-inner-appcall`

- **target-pinned-to-creation-state** ×6 — e.g. `app_3100284609.teal:1124`: caller asserts gtxnsa Applications 1/2 == "POOL_ID"/"FARM_ID" (written only on the creation call) for the same group index passed into the callee *Fixable: the caller's pin on gtxnsa Applications N is lost when the callee re-reads the slot.*
- **creator-pin-via-callee-bool** ×1 — e.g. `app_2002410770.teal:355`: label19 starts with txn Sender; callsub label26 (returns Sender == CreatorAddress); assert — the sender IS pinned, through a callee returning the comparison

## Policy labels

These classes are labelled by policy; a cell departs only through a
written override, listed here.

- `delete-funds-check` / **ungated-delete-no-itxn** = TP
  - override: `app_1050043795.teal:212` (delete-funds-check) → INTENDED: delete is the sale settlement and must be grouped with a sibling that closes the escrow (CloseRemainderTo pinned to global "ca"), which is where the funds sit
  - override: `app_1050043795.teal:354` (delete-funds-check) → INTENDED: delete is the sale settlement and must be grouped with a sibling that closes the escrow (CloseRemainderTo pinned to global "ca"), which is where the funds sit

## What TP/FP/INTENDED mean per detector

- `abi-method-selector`: TP = an approving exit reachable with arbitrary ApplicationArgs[0] (no selector match and not a bare NumAppArgs==0 route) that performs an action; FP = the exit is only reached after a selector match or a bare-route NumAppArgs==0 test, or is a create/opt-in/close-out OC path not meant to be method-dispatched; INTENDED = a deliberate catch-all/fallback handler.
- `arbitrary-inner-appcall`: TP = attacker chooses the called ApplicationID with app authority and no allowlist; FP = the id is checked; INTENDED = router/proxy design where the callee cannot abuse the app's authority.
- `arbitrary-inner-asset`: As tainted-fund-flow, for XferAsset: TP = attacker names an asset the app holds and it leaves the app with no check; INTENDED = the caller withdraws their own deposit of the asset they name, checked by per-user accounting; FP = the asset id is checked.
- `constant-condition`: TP = a branch condition that is really constant (dead code / always-taken check); FP = the condition is not constant.
- `delete-funds-check`: TP = Delete reachable by anyone with no balance handling — by POLICY also when the app issues no inner txns (class ungated-delete-no-itxn: its balance can never leave, so deleting strands it; a departure needs an explicit override); INTENDED = Delete gated to the creator/admin (the admin owns the stranding risk); FP = Delete cannot reach the exit, or the delete path drains the account (close-out inner txn).
- `group-size-check`: TP = an exit whose path relies on an absolute gtxn sibling with no GroupSize bound and no own-GroupIndex pin, so one sibling can be reused by several calls / padding changes the meaning; FP = the path to this exit reads no absolute gtxn, or GroupSize is in fact bounded, or the app pins its own GroupIndex such that padding cannot alter what was checked; UNKNOWN when the sibling's role cannot be judged.
- `hardcoded-min-balance`: TP = a hardcoded min-balance constant that is wrong for the asset/box usage; INTENDED = documented constant matching protocol MBR; FP = not a min-balance constant.
- `inner-txn-close-rekey`: TP = the close/rekey target is attacker-chosen (or the caller) on a path anyone can trigger and it drains a SHARED balance; INTENDED = target is the creator / a fixed address / a preserved admin key, or a per-user escrow closing to its owner; FP = the write is a provable no-op or cannot execute (e.g. closes to the app itself).
- `inner-txn-fee`: TP = a non-zero constant (or MinTxnFee) inner fee on a path any caller can trigger repeatedly without paying the app back; INTENDED = admin-only path, or the caller provably pays the app (sibling payment covering the fee); FP = the fee write is dead/overwritten.
- `is-deletable`: As is-updatable, for DeleteApplication.
- `is-updatable`: TP = an approving exit really reachable with OnCompletion=UpdateApplication and no sender gate; INTENDED = reachable but gated to the creator/a preserved admin; FP = Update cannot reach the exit with approval (OC excluded on every path, or the path always fails).
- `partial-tainted-fund-flow`: As tainted-fund-flow, for fund fields built from attacker-controlled byte slices.
- `tainted-asset-admin`: TP = attacker-chosen manager/reserve/freeze/clawback address in asset config; FP = checked; INTENDED = asset created for the caller (caller is the beneficiary).
- `tainted-freeze`: TP = attacker-chosen freeze target/asset with app authority; FP = checked; INTENDED = by design.
- `tainted-fund-flow`: TP = an attacker-chosen value reaches the inner-txn fund field (receiver/amount/asset/close) with no effective check in the attacker's disfavour; FP = a real check (sender pin, bound, equality to trusted state, the caller is the beneficiary of their own funds) neutralises it; INTENDED = the attacker-chosen value is the caller's OWN funds/receiver by design (withdraw your own balance to an address you name).
- `tainted-log`: TP = an attacker-chosen value logged where downstream consumers would trust it (ARC-28 event / return value claiming verification); INTENDED = logging the caller's own input (echo/ABI return of input) by design; FP = value is checked.
- `tainted-state-write`: TP = an attacker-chosen key/value written to state with no check that matters for the app's invariants; FP = a check (sender pin, constant set, bound) neutralises it; INTENDED = per-user state the caller is meant to set.
- `timelock-upgrade`: TP = an UNGATED Update path with no delay; INTENDED = admin/creator-gated Update without a delay (the author chose an instantly upgradable admin app); FP = Update cannot reach the exit, or a delay (round/timestamp comparison) gates it.
- `unprotected-deletable`: As unprotected-updatable, for DeleteApplication.
- `unprotected-updatable`: TP = Update reaches the exit with no effective sender authority check; FP = Update cannot reach it, or a real authority check (creator, preserved admin key, admin-signed sibling, fixed address) gates it; INTENDED = deliberately open upgrade (e.g. governance/immutable-by-other-means) evident from the code.
- `unsafe-division-order`: TP = integer division before multiplication loses precision in a value that matters (amounts/prices); FP = the division is exact by construction or the result does not feed a value; INTENDED = deliberate rounding (e.g. floor fee computation).
- `unvalidated-group-sibling`: TP = the app credits a sibling amount whose receiver is not pinned to an address the app controls (attacker can pay someone else/themselves); FP = the receiver is in fact pinned (by an equivalent check the detector missed) or the read amount is not used as a credit; INTENDED = benign by design (e.g. auction refund flows) where the rule holds but no loss follows.

## Staleness

Detector engines change; the labels do not. `python -m tests.mainnet_triage`
reports labels whose cell vanished (`resolved` — good for an FP, a
regression to explain for a TP) and new cells with no label
(`unlabelled`). `tests/test_mainnet_triage.py` fails only when a
detector with FP labels has a row on this page that no longer matches the
manifest + digest — regenerate with `--write-doc`.
